about:
Nemo Manufacturing Inc is an electronic contract manufacturer based in La Grange, Missouri. The company specializes in surface-mount (SMT) and through-hole (PTH) printed circuit board assemblies, offering services from prototype through production volumes.

Its capabilities include SMT and PTH assembly, cable assemblies, box builds, engineering prototypes, design-for-manufacturing assistance, and RoHS-compliant lead-free assembly. Nemo operates a lean manufacturing system that manages critical inventory and production scheduling, and it accepts both consigned and turnkey materials. Vendor approval and customer-supplied material acceptance programs are in place to maintain material integrity.

Customers range from prototype-stage developers to established OEMs requiring full production runs.

Nemo emphasizes its Six Sigma analytics integrated into an ISO 9001-certified quality management system, and its ability to navigate supply-chain disruptions such as allocations and long lead times. The firm highlights its Midwestern U.S.

name: Neocera LLC
old_description: Neocera is a technology company that serves academia, government and multinational companies that designs thin-film development products. Neocera offers a full range of solutions for thin films including pulsed laser deposition (PLD) systems, pulsed electron deposition (PED) systems, components and in situ diagnostic tools.
about:
Neocera LLC is headquartered in Beltsville, Maryland. The company was founded in 1989 by Dr. Venkatesan as a commercial vehicle for pulsed laser deposition (PLD) technology, focusing on complex multi-component metal-oxide thin film materials. Ownership details such as family, veteran, or woman-owned status are not publicly disclosed.

Neocera designs and manufactures pulsed laser deposition (PLD) systems, pulsed electron deposition (PED) systems, related components, and in-situ real-time diagnostic tools for thin-film development. The company describes itself as the largest supplier of PLD and PED tools for research and development, with experience integrating its systems with other deposition technologies and analytical equipment to create custom solutions. Facility size, headcount, and production volumes are not specified in the available information.

The company serves academia (universities), government (national research laboratories), and multinational corporations (corporate R&D centers). Its systems are installed in over 30 countries worldwide, supporting research and industrial applications in advanced materials.

Neocera states its mission is to become researchers' and manufacturers' first choice for PLD and PED equipment. The firm remains active in materials research, the application of PLD into new material systems and managing the transition of PLD processes from the laboratory to the industrial marketplace. Pulsed Electron Deposition was added as a complementary technique in 2001.

name: Neodesha Plastics Inc.
old_description: As a leading custom plastic manufacturing company, Neodesha Plastics specializes in custom plastic parts and manufacturing solutions. The advantages of working with a plastic forming company like ours include cost-effectiveness, efficiency, and the ability to serve a broad range of industries with tailored solutions. We’re an end-to-end partner for precision plastic manufacturing.
about:
Neodesha Plastics Inc. was founded in 1969 by Kenneth W. Peitz in Neodesha, Kansas. The family-owned company began in a 10,000-square-foot facility and has since expanded to over 165,000 square feet of production space in Southeast Kansas. It remains under Peitz family ownership with a long-tenured workforce.

The company provides full-service custom plastic manufacturing, including thermoforming (vacuum and pressure forming, deep-draw, twin-spindle rotary), CNC plastic machining (3-axis and 5-axis), rotational molding, plastic prototyping, and turnkey assembly and kitting. Its vertically integrated operation handles projects from one-off prototypes to runs of 10,000 finished goods, offering design-for-manufacturability feedback, tooling guidance, and material selection support.

Neodesha Plastics serves OEMs across automotive and transportation (instrument panels, chrome-laminated trims, modular kits), medical and life sciences (sterilizable housings, portable enclosures), marine and outdoor (UV-stable enclosures, fluid tanks, cup holders), and industrial and consumer markets (machine guards, trays, displays, ruggedized enclosures). Its central location enables shorter shipping timelines to the Midwest and beyond.

The company emphasizes its ISO 9001:2015-compliant quality system, domestic manufacturing, and integrated capabilities under one roof to reduce handoffs and accelerate delivery. Family ownership and a Midwest work ethic combine with modern automation to provide responsive service, flexible tooling, and value-added services such as drop-shipping.

about:
Netzer Metalworks, LLC operates from Essex, Maryland. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The shop provides CNC machining with 2-, 3-, and 4-axis milling and turning, sheet metal fabrication including punching, forming, rolling, and stretching, and welding services covering MIG, TIG, and spot welding. It also holds NADCAP accreditation for painting and powder coating, applying primer, topcoat, dry film, and powder coat finishes. Work encompasses large part envelopes and tight tolerances across a material palette that includes aluminum, stainless steel, nickel alloys such as Inconel, titanium, copper, composites, plastics, and carbon fibers. Additional capabilities include complex fabrications and assemblies, multi-part mechanical assembly, and hardware installation.

Customers span aerospace, defense, space, commercial aviation, food and beverage, medical, and general industrial sectors, all described as mission-critical industries.

Netzer Metalworks emphasizes its certified, accredited, and compliant status, with NADCAP-accredited finishing and a commitment to domestic manufacturing in the United States. Its focus on compliance and domestic production positions it for highly regulated programs.

name: Nev Metal Works, LLC
old_description: Nev Metal Works, LLC is your trusted source for custom metal fabrication services.
about:
Nev Metal Works, LLC operates from Winterset, Iowa, a small city southwest of Des Moines. The company was founded in 2007 by owners who wanted to combine a passion for metalworking with a commitment to first‑class fabrication services for the Des Moines metro area. It is structured as a veteran‑owned and family‑owned corporation.

The shop provides one‑stop fabrication services that span custom metal fabrication, contract manufacturing, welding repair, sign fabrication, and design. Its process lineup includes CNC plasma and laser cutting, CNC forming (with a 100‑ton, 10‑foot press brake), CNC machining, MIG, TIG, and stick welding of ferrous and non‑ferrous metals, CNC router cutting, saw cutting, and CAD/3D design programming. The company describes its facility as having the capabilities of a large production operation while retaining a small‑business approach to customer service.

Customers come from agriculture, construction, automotive, and furniture manufacturing, among other sectors. The company cites repairs on large farm, construction, and auto equipment as well as small interior metal furniture, and notes that it can reverse‑engineer and reproduce parts for any industry.

Nev Metal Works says it differentiates itself by being able to fabricate new parts for any process at any quantity, blending large‑corporation quality with small‑business personalization. An up‑front pricing policy and a mission to deliver products and service of the utmost quality are also highlighted as core principles.

about:
New Age Medical LLC is headquartered in Chesterfield, Missouri, and was founded in 2012 in nearby St. Louis with four employees and a vision to drive optimal patient outcomes. The company does not disclose its founders by name or its ownership structure beyond describing itself as a privately held business.

The firm operates as a self-described "MedTech hub" that connects medical device manufacturers, independent sales representatives, hospitals, ambulatory surgery centers, and surgeons. It provides FDA tissue intermediary services, runs an on-site training lab, and manages supply-chain and relationship logistics for spinal implants, orthobiologics, and related surgical products. The company states its national reach spans coast to coast, though it does not publish facility square footage, current headcount, or case volumes.

Its customer base includes manufacturers of spinal hardware and biologics, independent sales reps seeking portfolio expansion, surgeons looking for streamlined product access, and hospitals or ASCs aiming to improve efficiency. The platform emphasizes introducing new manufacturers based on surgeon feedback and clinical needs.

Leadership says the company was started to optimize the flow of medical solutions from manufacturer to patient. It differentiates itself by offering the extensive resources of a large organization while maintaining the agility and local decision-making of a small business, aiming to get partners what they need, when they need it.

name: New Deantronics
old_description: New Deantronics is a medical/surgical device developer & manufacturer founded in San Francisco, CA in 1985 with engineering and manufacturing operations located in Taiwan.
about:
New Deantronics was founded in 1985 in San Francisco, California, and now operates its U.S. headquarters from a 200,000-square-foot campus in Spanish Springs, Nevada, near Sparks. The company is led by CEO Jane Liu and maintains engineering and manufacturing operations in Taiwan.

The company develops and manufactures electrosurgical medical devices, including nano-scale cameras used in neurosurgery, orthopedics, cardiology, and general surgery. Its services span design, development, manufacturing, packaging, sterilization, and regulatory support. The new Nevada facility houses research, development, and production under one roof, alongside a medical device incubation center for start-ups. Advanced facilities in Taiwan also include incubation centers.

New Deantronics serves the global medical device industry, supplying devices for general surgery, neurosurgery, cardiology, orthopedics, and aesthetics. Its customers include hospitals and surgical centers using radio frequency-based instruments, as well as early-stage medical device companies accessing the incubation center.

The company states its mission is to advance healthcare and quality of life for patients through medical/surgical technology. It emphasizes quality products, attention to detail, social responsibility, timely delivery, and fair prices as core values, and differentiates itself with an end-to-end service model and a dedicated incubation center for medical device start-ups.

name: New England Wire Technologies
old_description: Explore our comprehensive range of wire and cable solutions for various industries and applications.
about:
New England Wire Technologies is based in Lisbon, New Hampshire. The company traces its origins to 1898, when it began as a local wire producer. Over more than a century it has grown into a global engineering partner while remaining headquartered in the same town.

The company designs and manufactures custom wire and cable solutions, including high‑performance Litz wire for high‑frequency applications, multi‑conductor cables for data transmission and power distribution, hybrid cable configurations, and custom tubing for medical, aerospace, and industrial uses. Operations are carried out in manufacturing facilities and testing labs in Lisbon, though the company does not disclose facility size, headcount, or annual volumes.

Its customers span medical device makers, aerospace contractors, and industrial equipment manufacturers. The firm also serves broader markets through subsidiaries: New England Tubing Technologies in Lisbon, Bay Associates Wire Technologies (operating as BayCable) in Fremont, California, and New England Interconnect Systems in Santa Ana, Mexico.

The business was founded on the principle of solving problems that others won’t attempt. It emphasizes engineer‑to‑engineer collaboration, translating complex tolerances and material choices into practical designs, and building long‑term partnerships through candor and custom engineering rather than off‑the‑shelf products.

name: New Jersey Textiles
old_description: For close to 70 years, New Jersey Textiles, Inc. (previously known as D&M Textiles) has been supplying wholesale fabrics at closeout prices to the U.S. market. We service retail stores, manufacturers, decorators, designers and the home rug hooking trade.
about:
New Jersey Textiles, Inc. traces its roots to 1945, when Israel Merdinger and his son Julius arrived in the United States from Poland and entered the rag trade in New York City. Starting with a hand truck, they collected wool clippings from garment factories in the Garment Center and transported them to what would become SoHo, eventually leasing warehouse space and purchasing a building to sort and bale the waste for export to overseas mills. The business later relocated to Clifton, New Jersey, where it operates today under the leadership of President David Merdinger.

The company functions as a wholesale fabric distributor, purchasing closeout and excess inventory from clothing manufacturers and jobbers throughout the New York–New Jersey metropolitan area. Its stock turns constantly and is sold by the yard, by the bolt, or by the pound. Current offerings include print chiffons, ITY prints, taffetas, and laces. In addition to fabric wholesaling, New Jersey Textiles continues to import and export wool clippings for reprocessing.

Customers span retail stores, apparel manufacturers, interior decorators, designers, and the home rug‑hooking trade across the United States. The firm positions itself as a low‑cost source for short‑run and specialty fabrics, with no minimum order mentioned in its public materials.

The operation began as a family effort to build a livelihood from post‑war textile waste, evolving over decades into a dual‑track business that both recycles wool by‑products and supplies discounted yard goods to a broad base of buyers.
